description: Detects an interactive browser OAuth sign-in to Azure CLI or other developer-tool first-party applications, the fingerprint of the ConsentFix localhost-callback consent lure.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/consentfix-and-clickfix-how-microsoft-365-accounts-are-hijacked-in-3-seconds/
  - https://pushsecurity.com/blog/consentfix
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/03
tags:
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.t1550.001
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    AppId:
      - '04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46'
      - '1950a258-227b-4e31-a9cf-717495945fc2'
      - 'aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56'
      - '04f0c124-f2bc-4f59-8241-bf6df9866bbd'
      - '12128f48-ec9e-42f0-b203-ea49fb6af367'
    IsInteractive: true
    ResultType: 0
    ClientAppUsed: 'Browser'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.appDisplayName:("Microsoft Azure CLI" OR "Microsoft Azure PowerShell" OR "Visual Studio Code" OR "Microsoft Visual Studio" OR "Microsoft Teams PowerShell Cmdlets")
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where (Authentication.app IN ("04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46","1950a258-227b-4e31-a9cf-717495945fc2","aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56","04f0c124-f2bc-4f59-8241-bf6df9866bbd","12128f48-ec9e-42f0-b203-ea49fb6af367")) by Authentication.user Authentication.app Authentication.src Authentication.action _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where action="success" | convert ctime(firstTime) | convert ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where (Authentication.app IN ("04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46","1950a258-227b-4e31-a9cf-717495945fc2","aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56","04f0c124-f2bc-4f59-8241-bf6df9866bbd","12128f48-ec9e-42f0-b203-ea49fb6af367")) by Authentication.user Authentication.app Authentication.src Authentication.action _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where action="success" | convert ctime(firstTime) | convert ctime(lastTime)
ConsentFix: Azure CLI token redemption from divergent IP within 10 min of interactive sign-in AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates the two sign-in events ConsentFix produces for a single OAuth authorization-code theft: the victim's interactive sign-in to a dev-tool first-party app, followed by a non-interactive token redemption for the same user/app from a different IP within ~10 minutes. Human-delayed, geographically-dispersed redemption distinguishes the attack from legitimate CLI use (same IP, seconds). Rationale: Directly encodes Push Security's ConsentFix detection: two sign-ins sharing UserId+AppId, second within ~10 min, divergent IPs (legitimate CLI redeems within seconds from the same IP). App IDs and the 10-minute/divergent-IP heuristic are corroborated across Push Security and gblock write-ups. Datadog query is the base scope; IP-divergence + 10-min grouping is set at rule level. Cross-checked against: • https://pushsecurity.com/blog/consentfix • https://www.gblock.app/articles/consentfix-v3-azure-cli-oauth-microsoft-365-phishing • https://www.mitiga.io/blog/consentfix-oauth-phishing-explained-how-token-based-attacks-bypass-mfa-in-microsoft-entra-id
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1528
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Roaming/VPN user whose interactive login and token redemption egress via different IPs
  • Mobile hotspot failover changing the source IP between sign-in and token refresh
  • CI/CD or automation redeeming an Azure CLI code from a build agent for a legitimate service context
  • Corporate proxy pool assigning different egress IPs to auth vs Graph calls
  • Legitimate cross-region Azure Cloud Shell usage by a developer
Suppression filter
| where RedeemCountry != VictimCountry or DelaySec > 30   // suppress same-country sub-30s redemptions typical of legit CLI/Cloud Shell
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Compare VictimIP vs RedeemIP geolocation/ASN and DelaySec; a >30s delay with a foreign or hosting-provider ASN redemption is high-signal. Confirm the user is not a routine CLI user. Step 2 (contain): Immediately revoke sign-in sessions and refresh tokens for the AccountObjectId, block the RedeemIP, and disable the account pending review. Step 3 (hunt): Enumerate all activity from the attacker session (mailbox reads, new inbox/forwarding rules, added app consents, Graph directory enumeration) and sweep other users for interactive sign-ins to the same AppScope.
let AppScope = dynamic(["04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46","1950a258-227b-4e31-a9cf-717495945fc2","aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56","04f0c124-f2bc-4f59-8241-bf6df9866bbd","12128f48-ec9e-42f0-b203-ea49fb6af367"]);
let Interactive = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ApplicationId in (AppScope)
    | where IsInteractive == true and ErrorCode == 0
    | project VictimTime = Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountUpn, ApplicationId, VictimIP = IPAddress, VictimCountry = Country;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ApplicationId in (AppScope)
| where IsInteractive == false and ErrorCode == 0
| project RedeemTime = Timestamp, AccountObjectId, ApplicationId, RedeemIP = IPAddress, RedeemCountry = Country, RedeemUserAgent = UserAgent
| join kind=inner Interactive on AccountObjectId, ApplicationId
| where RedeemTime between (VictimTime .. VictimTime + 10m)   // 10-min human-delayed redemption window (Push Security)
| where RedeemIP != VictimIP                                  // attacker infra differs from victim device
| project VictimTime, RedeemTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', RedeemTime, VictimTime), AccountUpn, ApplicationId, VictimIP, VictimCountry, RedeemIP, RedeemCountry, RedeemUserAgent
| order by VictimTime desc
let AppScope = dynamic(["04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46","1950a258-227b-4e31-a9cf-717495945fc2","aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56","04f0c124-f2bc-4f59-8241-bf6df9866bbd","12128f48-ec9e-42f0-b203-ea49fb6af367"]);
let Interactive = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where AppId in (AppScope)
    | where IsInteractive == true and ResultType == 0
    | project VictimTime = TimeGenerated, UserId, UserPrincipalName, AppId, VictimIP = IPAddress, VictimLoc = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion);
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where AppId in (AppScope)
| where ResultType == 0
| project RedeemTime = TimeGenerated, UserId, AppId, RedeemIP = IPAddress, RedeemUA = UserAgent
| join kind=inner Interactive on UserId, AppId
| where RedeemTime between (VictimTime .. VictimTime + 10m)   // 10-min human-delayed redemption window
| where RedeemIP != VictimIP
| project VictimTime, RedeemTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', RedeemTime, VictimTime), UserPrincipalName, AppId, VictimIP, VictimLoc, RedeemIP, RedeemUA
| order by VictimTime desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.appDisplayName:("Microsoft Azure CLI" OR "Microsoft Azure PowerShell" OR "Visual Studio Code")
ClickFix: PowerShell/mshta download-execute spawned from Run dialog (explorer parent) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the ClickFix execution step where the victim pastes an attacker command into the Windows Run dialog after a fake CAPTCHA/verification prompt, causing PowerShell, mshta, cmd or curl to launch as a child of explorer.exe with download-and-execute arguments. Targets the article's explicit recommendation to detect 'unusual PowerShell activity originating from normal user processes.' Rationale: ClickFix pastes the payload into the Win+R Run dialog, so the interpreter's parent is explorer.exe (not Office, which is separately covered). Pairing that parent anomaly with download-execute cmdline tokens is the article's named signal ('unusual PowerShell from normal user processes') and avoids the excluded Office-spawns-script / encoded-PowerShell rules. Cross-checked against: • https://pushsecurity.com/blog/consentfix • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/consentfix-and-clickfix-how-microsoft-365-accounts-are-hijacked-in-3-seconds/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1204 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin manually pasting an Invoke-WebRequest one-liner into Run for legitimate tooling install
  • Software deployment scripts triggered via a Run-dialog shortcut
  • Developer using curl.exe from Run to test an endpoint
  • Help-desk remote-guidance walking a user through a PowerShell command
  • Legitimate .hta-based internal application launched by double-click
Suppression filter
| where not(AccountName in~ ("admin","helpdesk") and DeviceName has_any ("IT-","ADMIN-"))   // suppress known admin build/support hosts after tuning
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and resolve the URL/host it fetches; check if the user reported a CAPTCHA/'verify you are human' prompt just prior. Inspect any child process and dropped file (SHA256). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the endpoint, kill the process tree, and block the fetched domain/IP at proxy/EDR. Step 3 (hunt): Search the same host and user for follow-on stager execution, new persistence (Run keys/scheduled tasks), and — critically — subsequent interactive Azure CLI sign-ins (UC1) indicating the ClickFix chained into ConsentFix.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"   // Win+R Run dialog / double-click origin
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("iwr","invoke-webrequest","iex","invoke-expression","downloadstring","downloadfile","mshta http","-w hidden","-windowstyle hidden","-nop","frombase64string",".hta","curl ","certutil","start-bitstransfer","http://","https://")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("iwr","invoke-webrequest","iex","downloadstring","downloadfile","mshta http","-w hidden","-windowstyle hidden","-nop","frombase64string",".hta","curl ","certutil","http://","https://")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ClickFix Run-Dialog Download-Execute via Explorer-Spawned Interpreter
id: b2e4d3c5-6f7a-4b8d-8e9f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
description: Detects PowerShell/mshta/cmd/curl launched from explorer.exe (Run dialog) with download-and-execute arguments, the ClickFix paste-and-run execution step.
references:

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'iwr'
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'IEX'
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'mshta http'
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-windowstyle hidden'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - '.hta'
      - 'certutil'
      - 'http'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\Explorer.exe OR *\\EXPLORER.EXE) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\curl.exe) @CommandLine:(*iwr* OR *Invoke-WebRequest* OR *IEX* OR *DownloadString* OR *"mshta http"* OR *"-w hidden"* OR *FromBase64String* OR *.hta* OR *certutil* OR *http*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|mshta|cmd|curl|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(iwr|invoke-webrequest|iex|downloadstring|downloadfile|mshta http|-w hidden|-windowstyle hidden|frombase64string|\\.hta|certutil|https?://)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe") (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")) (Processes.process IN ("*iwr*","*invoke-webrequest*","*IEX*","*DownloadString*","*DownloadFile*","*mshta http*","*-w hidden*","*-windowstyle hidden*","*FromBase64String*","*.hta*","*curl *","*certutil*","*http://*","*https://*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | convert ctime(firstTime) | convert ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe") (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")) (Processes.process IN ("*iwr*","*invoke-webrequest*","*IEX*","*DownloadString*","*DownloadFile*","*mshta http*","*-w hidden*","*-windowstyle hidden*","*FromBase64String*","*.hta*","*curl *","*certutil*","*http://*","*https://*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | convert ctime(firstTime) | convert ctime(lastTime)
ConsentFix lure delivery: inbound email link to DocSend/Dropbox or ConsentFix phishing infra AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the ConsentFix delivery stage: inbound, delivered email carrying a link to DocSend/Dropbox (often password-protected to evade inspection) or to the campaign's phishing infrastructure. Surfaces the lure before the victim reaches the fake Microsoft sign-in page. Rationale: Article names Dropbox/DocSend as the trusted-platform delivery channel (often password-protected); Push Security supplies corroborated ConsentFix payload domains (trustpointassurance.com, fastwaycheck.com, previewcentral.com) which I use as high-fidelity infra IOCs, plus the article's security-updater.com. Generic Dropbox/DocSend is tiered hunting due to legitimate-use noise; the infra-domain lookups are alert-grade. Cross-checked against: • https://pushsecurity.com/blog/consentfix • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/consentfix-and-clickfix-how-microsoft-365-accounts-are-hijacked-in-3-seconds/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate business use of DocSend for sales/investor documents
  • Genuine Dropbox file-share links between partners
  • Marketing or vendor newsletters linking to Dropbox-hosted assets
  • Password-protected but benign contract shares from a real counterparty
  • Internal team sharing large files via a Dropbox link
Suppression filter
| where not(SenderMailFromDomain in~ ("docsend.com","dropbox.com") and Verdict == "trusted-service-lure")   // drop platform-native notification mails; keep third-party-sent links
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For ConsentFix-infra hits, treat as confirmed-bad and identify all recipients; for DocSend/Dropbox hits, check sender reputation, SPF/DKIM/DMARC in AuthenticationDetails, and whether the landing page renders a Microsoft sign-in. Step 2 (contain): Soft-delete/quarantine the message tenant-wide (ZAP), block the infra domains at mail/proxy, and warn recipients not to interact. Step 3 (hunt): Correlate recipients against UrlClickEvents and subsequent interactive Azure CLI sign-ins (UC1) and ClickFix executions (UC3) to find anyone who progressed past delivery.
let LureDomains = dynamic(["docsend.com","dropbox.com","dropboxusercontent.com"]);
let ConsentFixInfra = dynamic(["trustpointassurance.com","fastwaycheck.com","previewcentral.com","security-updater.com"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
| join kind=inner (
    EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| where UrlDomain has_any (LureDomains) or UrlDomain has_any (ConsentFixInfra)
| extend Verdict = iff(UrlDomain has_any (ConsentFixInfra), "ConsentFix-infra", "trusted-service-lure")
| project Timestamp, Verdict, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, Url, UrlDomain, AuthenticationDetails
| order by Timestamp desc
let ConsentFixInfra = dynamic(["docsend.com","trustpointassurance.com","fastwaycheck.com","previewcentral.com","security-updater.com"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Url has_any (ConsentFixInfra)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname, HttpStatusCode
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Post-session-theft mailbox abuse: auto-forwarding / inbox rule creation via stolen M365 session AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the actions-on-objective stage after ConsentFix session theft: the attacker uses the stolen token (no password, MFA bypassed) to create mailbox forwarding or inbox rules that exfiltrate or hide mail. Targets the article's stated impact — 'session access to email' — and the hidden-rule tradecraft typical of OAuth-token account takeover. Rationale: The article's stated impact is session access to email; token-theft account takeovers routinely pivot to auto-forwarding/hiding rules. Keys on Exchange audit operations (New-InboxRule/Set-Mailbox) with forwarding/deletion parameters — high-fidelity when the initiating IP/UserAgent diverges from the user's baseline (pairs with UC1/UC2). Cross-checked against: • https://pushsecurity.com/blog/consentfix • https://www.mitiga.io/blog/consentfix-oauth-phishing-explained-how-token-based-attacks-bypass-mfa-in-microsoft-entra-id
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1564.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User legitimately setting up out-of-office forwarding to a delegate
  • Admin configuring a mailbox forward during offboarding
  • Power user creating an inbox rule to file newsletters into a folder
  • Migration tooling adjusting mailbox delivery settings
  • Executive assistant setting redirect rules on a shared mailbox
Suppression filter
and RawEventData has_any ("ForwardTo","RedirectTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo") and RawEventData !has "@yourtenantdomain.com"   // keep only rules forwarding OUTSIDE the org (replace yourtenantdomain.com per tenant)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the rule's target — external ForwardTo/RedirectTo addresses or DeleteMessage on security-sender mail is high-signal; compare ClientIP/UserAgent to the user's baseline and to any UC1/UC2 anomalous Azure CLI sign-in. Step 2 (contain): Disable/remove the rule, revoke the user's sessions and refresh tokens, and block the external forward address. Step 3 (hunt): Review the mailbox for read/exfil activity, other tenant users with new forwarding rules in the same window, and OAuth app consents granted from the same session.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules","Set-Mailbox","New-TransportRule")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeliverToMailboxAndForward","DeleteMessage","MoveToFolder")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, ActionType, Application, IPAddress, CountryCode, UserAgent, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Operation in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules","Set-Mailbox","New-TransportRule")
| where Parameters has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeliverToMailboxAndForward","DeleteMessage")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, ClientIP, OriginatingServer, Parameters
| order by TimeGenerated desc

level: high
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)

| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ToddyCat-Linked Umbrij Malware Abuses OAuth to Access Gmail via Google API

The Hacker News
2026-07-02 16 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The threat actor known as ToddyCat has been attributed to a new malware called Umbrij that's designed to gain surreptitious access to a victim's email correspondence via the Google API. "In this campaign, the attackers focused their attention on corporate email communications hosted on Gmail, targeting access compromise via APIs," Kaspersky said in a detailed report published this week. "

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — ToddyCat-Linked Umbrij Malware Abuses OAuth to Access Gmail via Google API
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] ToddyCat Umbrij DLL side-loading via signed BDSubWiz/VSTestVideoRecorder/GoogleDesktop · [LLM] Scheduled task masquerading as Kaspersky EDR ('KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp') · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Headless Chromium remote-debugging launched against copied BackupFiles profile (STRD) · [LLM] Google OAuth endpoint reached by browser spawned from Umbrij side-load binary
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Browser credential store copied into %LOCALAPPDATA% BackupFiles staging directory · [LLM] OAuth grant / API access to 'Google Workspace Migration for Microsoft Outlook' app (Umbrij token abuse) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
ToddyCat Umbrij DLL side-loading via signed BDSubWiz/VSTestVideoRecorder/GoogleDesktop AIInstallation High
Hunts the specific DLL side-loading chain ToddyCat uses to launch the Umbrij .NET stealer: three legitimate signed binaries each insecurely loading a named rogue DLL. Article-specific because it pairs each abused host binary with its exact malicious module name and hash rather than generic side-loading. Rationale: Uses the exact abused host binaries (BDSubWiz.exe/VSTestVideoRecorder.exe/GoogleDesktop.exe), their paired rogue DLL names, the Umbrij DLL MD5s (28cb7b26.../bae82a15.../9f5f2f0f...), and the anomalous drop paths confirmed by Securelist. The binary+DLL pairing is near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/toddycat-apt-umbrij-tool-and-oauth/120251/ • https://gbhackers.com/toddycat-uses-shadow-token/ • https://cyberpress.org/toddycat-automates-gmail-compromise/
ATT&CKT1574.001 T1134.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Bitdefender ConnectAgent running BDSubWiz.exe from its real Program Files path (excluded by anomalous-path filter)
  • Genuine Visual Studio test agent running VSTestVideoRecorder.exe from the VS install tree
  • A developer manually placing a signed tool in C:\Users\Public for testing
  • Security tooling copying signed binaries to Temp during sandbox detonation
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\Program Files\Bitdefender" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\Microsoft Visual Studio\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the loading binary runs from Temp/Vss/Public and the loaded DLL name/hash matches (log.dll, GoogleServices.dll, or the VideoRecorderEngine DLL). Pull the DLL and check signer/ConfuserEx obfuscation. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the side-loading process, quarantine the rogue DLL and the co-located signed EXE. 3) Hunt: search the same host and user for the scheduled task 'KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp', a %LOCALAPPDATA%\...\BackupFiles directory, and headless-browser remote-debugging launches (UC3/UC4).
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("BDSubWiz.exe","VSTestVideoRecorder.exe","GoogleDesktop.exe")
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "BDSubWiz.exe" and FileName =~ "log.dll")
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "VSTestVideoRecorder.exe" and FileName =~ "Microsoft.VisualStudio.QualityTools.VideoRecorderEngine.dll")
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "GoogleDesktop.exe" and FileName =~ "GoogleServices.dll")
    or MD5 in~ ("28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1","bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66","9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, LoadedDll = FileName, LoadedDllPath = FolderPath, MD5, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel has no native image-load table; pivot on the host binary executing from an anomalous location (Umbrij drop paths)
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("BDSubWiz.exe","VSTestVideoRecorder.exe","GoogleDesktop.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any (@"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Windows\Vss\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Scheduled task masquerading as Kaspersky EDR ('KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp') AIInstallation High
Hunts the persistence/execution primitive Umbrij used: a scheduled task named after Kaspersky's EDR agent that launches the digitally signed side-loading binary. Article-specific because it keys on the exact impersonated task name Kaspersky reported during its threat hunt. Rationale: Keys on the exact impersonated task name 'KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp' reported by Kaspersky; a scheduled task with that name not created by a genuine Kaspersky process is an unambiguous ToddyCat indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/toddycat-apt-umbrij-tool-and-oauth/120251/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine Kaspersky Endpoint Security installer/updater registering its own EDR task (excluded by initiating-process filter)
  • Backup/imaging tools cloning a host that legitimately runs Kaspersky and replaying task XML
  • Sysadmin manually re-creating a Kaspersky task after repair
  • SCCM/Intune redeploying Kaspersky agent
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\Kaspersky Lab\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the task action/XML — confirm it launches a signed binary (BDSubWiz/VSTestVideoRecorder/GoogleDesktop) from Temp/Vss/Public rather than the real Kaspersky path, and identify the creating process. 2) Contain: delete the rogue task, isolate the host, quarantine the referenced binary+DLL. 3) Hunt: correlate to UC1 (side-load), and check for BackupFiles browser-profile copies and headless remote-debugging launches on the same host/user.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "ScheduledTaskCreated"
| where AdditionalFields has "KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp" or ProcessCommandLine has "KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("avp.exe","kavfsslp.exe")   // exclude genuine Kaspersky-created tasks
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4698   // scheduled task created
| where EventData has "KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Headless Chromium remote-debugging launched against copied BackupFiles profile (STRD) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the core Shadow Token via Remote Debug (STRD) step: Umbrij launches Chrome/Edge headless with a remote debugging port pointed at a copied user profile in BackupFiles to hijack the live Gmail session. Article-specific via the exact flag+path combination. Rationale: Combines the exact Chromium flag (--remote-debugging-port) with the article's attacker-specific staging folder 'BackupFiles'; no legitimate workflow launches a browser headless-debugging against a copied BackupFiles profile. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/toddycat-apt-umbrij-tool-and-oauth/120251/ • https://gbhackers.com/toddycat-uses-shadow-token/
ATT&CKT1185 T1550.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Puppeteer/Playwright automated UI test suites launching headless Chrome with remote-debugging (won't reference BackupFiles)
  • Selenium/browser-automation CI runners on developer endpoints
  • Manual developer debugging with --remote-debugging-port against a normal profile path
  • Enterprise screenshot/monitoring tools driving Chrome headless
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("node.exe","python.exe","pwsh.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has "BackupFiles"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm --user-data-dir points into a BackupFiles folder and identify the parent process (expect a side-load binary). Grep the host for the Umbrij log file containing an OAuth authorization code. 2) Contain: kill the browser+parent, isolate host, and initiate Google Workspace token revocation for the affected user. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC5 (OAuth network flow) and UC6 (Google Workspace Migration/Sync app grant) for the same user, and revoke sessions in Google Admin.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--remote-debugging-port"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "BackupFiles"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--remote-debugging-port"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "BackupFiles"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

  - attack.t1550.001
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--remote-debugging-port'
      - 'BackupFiles'
  condition: selection_img and selection_flags
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\MSEdge.exe)) @CommandLine:*remote-debugging-port* @CommandLine:*BackupFiles*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/--remote-debugging-port/i
| CommandLine=/BackupFiles/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe") AND Processes.process="*--remote-debugging-port*" AND Processes.process="*BackupFiles*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe") AND Processes.process="*--remote-debugging-port*" AND Processes.process="*BackupFiles*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Browser credential store copied into %LOCALAPPDATA% BackupFiles staging directory AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts Umbrij's profile-theft step: copying Login Data, Web Data, cookies and Local/IndexedDB storage of each authenticated profile into a BackupFiles directory under the Chrome/Edge app-data path. Article-specific via the exact folder and the named profile artifacts. Rationale: Keys on the exact attacker-created 'BackupFiles' subfolder under the Chrome/Edge LocalAppData path plus the named profile artifacts (Login Data, Web Data, cookies, IndexedDB); browsers never write those files into a BackupFiles directory, and the non-browser initiating process makes it high fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/toddycat-apt-umbrij-tool-and-oauth/120251/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A backup/migration utility that literally names its folder 'BackupFiles' and copies browser profiles (rare; verify initiating process)
  • Browser profile-migration tools during OS upgrade
  • IT-driven roaming-profile sync copying Login Data
  • User manually backing up a browser profile into a folder coincidentally named BackupFiles
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","browsermigration.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process that wrote into BackupFiles (expect a side-load binary, not chrome/msedge) and enumerate which profiles/emails were staged. 2) Contain: isolate host, remove the BackupFiles directory after forensic capture, and force-reset the affected user's browser sessions and Google Workspace tokens. 3) Hunt: correlate to UC3 headless remote-debug launch and UC6 Google Workspace app grant on the same user; assume cookie/session theft and rotate.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "BackupFiles"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Login Data For Account","Web Data","Preferences","Secure Preferences","Cookies") or FolderPath has_any ("IndexedDB","Local Storage","Network")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "BackupFiles"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("Login Data","Web Data","Preferences","Secure Preferences","IndexedDB","Local Storage","Network","Cookies")
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Browser Credential Store Copied to BackupFiles Directory (Umbrij)
id: e1d4a70b-3c56-4f92-a0b8-2d9f7c1e6a44
description: Detects creation of Chrome/Edge credential and session artifacts inside a BackupFiles staging directory under the browser local-app-data path, used by Umbrij to stage profiles for headless session hijack.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/toddycat-apt-umbrij-tool-and-oauth/120251/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/03
tags:
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Google\Chrome\BackupFiles\'
      - '\Microsoft\Edge\BackupFiles\'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\Chrome\BackupFiles\* OR *\chrome\BackupFiles\* OR *\Edge\BackupFiles\* OR *\edge\BackupFiles\*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\(Chrome|Edge)\\BackupFiles\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\BackupFiles\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Microsoft\\Edge\\BackupFiles\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\BackupFiles\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Microsoft\\Edge\\BackupFiles\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Google OAuth endpoint reached by browser spawned from Umbrij side-load binary AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the STRD token-acquisition network step: a Chrome/Edge process spawned by one of the abused side-load host binaries contacts accounts.google.com / oauth2.googleapis.com to drive the OAuth consent-and-token flow. Article-specific via the parent-process chain, not generic Google traffic. Rationale: The fidelity comes from the parent chain — a browser spawned by BDSubWiz/VSTestVideoRecorder/GoogleDesktop hitting Google OAuth endpoints — plus the specific client project IDs 279448736670/1095133494869 (Google Workspace Migration/Sync for Outlook) in the proxy URL where available; plain accounts.google.com traffic alone is filtered out by the parent predicate. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/toddycat-apt-umbrij-tool-and-oauth/120251/ • https://cyberpress.org/toddycat-automates-gmail-compromise/
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1185
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Normal user browsing to accounts.google.com (excluded — requires side-load parent or remote-debugging flag)
  • Legit Google Workspace Migration/Sync for Outlook actually deployed and used by the org (validate at myaccount.google.com/connections)
  • Browser automation frameworks authenticating to Google
  • Enterprise SSO flows to oauth2.googleapis.com
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "BackupFiles" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("BDSubWiz.exe","VSTestVideoRecorder.exe","GoogleDesktop.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the browser's parent is a side-load host binary (or the remote-debugging flag is present) and capture the full OAuth URL/client_id from proxy logs. 2) Contain: isolate host, and in Google Admin revoke the 'Google Workspace Migration/Sync for Microsoft Outlook' authorization and force token/session invalidation for the user. 3) Hunt: search UC6 for subsequent Gmail/Drive/Contacts API access via that app, and check the Umbrij log file for the exfiltrated authorization code.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("accounts.google.com","oauth2.googleapis.com")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("BDSubWiz.exe","VSTestVideoRecorder.exe","GoogleDesktop.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--remote-debugging-port"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc
// Requires web-proxy telemetry that captures the full OAuth request URL/query
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "accounts.google.com/o/oauth2" or Url has "oauth2.googleapis.com"
| where Url has_any ("279448736670","1095133494869")   // Google Workspace Migration / Sync for Outlook client project IDs
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\MSEdge.exe)) (@DestinationHostname:accounts.google.com OR @DestinationHostname:oauth2.googleapis.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(accounts\.google\.com|oauth2\.googleapis\.com)$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | ParentBaseFileName=/\\?(BDSubWiz|VSTestVideoRecorder|GoogleDesktop)\.exe$/i | ImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge)\.exe$/i}, field=[ContextProcessId], key=[TargetProcessId], include=[ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("BDSubWiz.exe","VSTestVideoRecorder.exe","GoogleDesktop.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("BDSubWiz.exe","VSTestVideoRecorder.exe","GoogleDesktop.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
OAuth grant / API access to 'Google Workspace Migration for Microsoft Outlook' app (Umbrij token abuse) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the objective of the STRD attack: an OAuth authorization and subsequent Gmail/Drive/Contacts API access via the Google Workspace Migration or Sync for Microsoft Outlook application, whose client IDs Umbrij drives to mint tokens. Article-specific via the exact abused app names and client project IDs. Rationale: Uses the exact application names ('Google Workspace Migration/Sync for Microsoft Outlook') Kaspersky told defenders to look for at myaccount.google.com/connections, plus the corroborated client project IDs 279448736670/1095133494869; token grants to these apps in an org that doesn't use them are a direct Umbrij indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/toddycat-apt-umbrij-tool-and-oauth/120251/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/toddycat-linked-umbrij-malware-abuses.html
ATT&CKT1528 T1550.001 T1114.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Org genuinely migrating mailboxes from Exchange/Outlook into Google Workspace (validate with IT — legitimate Migration tool use)
  • Users who legitimately run Google Workspace Sync for Microsoft Outlook
  • Admin-approved third-party marketplace OAuth apps with similar scopes
  • A one-off sanctioned data-import project
Response runbook
1) Triage: at myaccount.google.com/connections (or Google Admin > Security > API controls) confirm whether the Migration/Sync app is sanctioned; review IP/geo/user-agent and the granted Gmail/Drive/Contacts/Calendar scopes. 2) Contain: if unsanctioned, revoke the app's access to invalidate all issued OAuth tokens and force-reauth the user. 3) Hunt: enumerate all users who granted the same app, review Gmail API read volume (users.messages.list/get) for bulk export, and correlate to the endpoint chain (UC1–UC5).
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has_any ("Google Workspace Migration for Microsoft Outlook","Google Workspace Sync for Microsoft Outlook")
    or ObjectName has_any ("Google Workspace Migration for Microsoft Outlook","Google Workspace Sync for Microsoft Outlook")
    or AdditionalFields has_any ("279448736670","1095133494869")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, Application, ActionType, ActivityType, IPAddress, CountryCode, ISP, UserAgent, ObjectName, IsAnonymousProxy
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Application has_any ("Google Workspace Migration for Microsoft Outlook","Google Workspace Sync for Microsoft Outlook")
    or ObjectName has_any ("Google Workspace Migration for Microsoft Outlook","Google Workspace Sync for Microsoft Outlook")
    or AdditionalFields has_any ("279448736670","1095133494869")
| project TimeGenerated, AccountDisplayName, Application, ActionType, ActivityType, IPAddress, CountryCode, ISP, UserAgent, ObjectName, IsAnonymousProxy
| order by TimeGenerated desc
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1ab58838e5790efb22f2d35ab98c0b7d", "a7d7d6c4c3f227f7117261c63b9e23a9", "3d3a621f852c42d97fd7260681e42508", "3432dd9ac0df80ef86eb80bd080f839b", "22aaeb4946ba6d2f2e27feb7dbb295de", "f61fbfb7aa1cd5dc8f70b055b51563e2", "f169d6d172dfb775895a5e2b1540c854", "9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f", "28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1", "bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66") or SHA1 in~ ("1ab58838e5790efb22f2d35ab98c0b7d", "a7d7d6c4c3f227f7117261c63b9e23a9", "3d3a621f852c42d97fd7260681e42508", "3432dd9ac0df80ef86eb80bd080f839b", "22aaeb4946ba6d2f2e27feb7dbb295de", "f61fbfb7aa1cd5dc8f70b055b51563e2", "f169d6d172dfb775895a5e2b1540c854", "9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f", "28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1", "bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66") or MD5 in~ ("1ab58838e5790efb22f2d35ab98c0b7d", "a7d7d6c4c3f227f7117261c63b9e23a9", "3d3a621f852c42d97fd7260681e42508", "3432dd9ac0df80ef86eb80bd080f839b", "22aaeb4946ba6d2f2e27feb7dbb295de", "f61fbfb7aa1cd5dc8f70b055b51563e2", "f169d6d172dfb775895a5e2b1540c854", "9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f", "28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1", "bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),

        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1ab58838e5790efb22f2d35ab98c0b7d", "a7d7d6c4c3f227f7117261c63b9e23a9", "3d3a621f852c42d97fd7260681e42508", "3432dd9ac0df80ef86eb80bd080f839b", "22aaeb4946ba6d2f2e27feb7dbb295de", "f61fbfb7aa1cd5dc8f70b055b51563e2", "f169d6d172dfb775895a5e2b1540c854", "9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f", "28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1", "bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66") or SHA1 in~ ("1ab58838e5790efb22f2d35ab98c0b7d", "a7d7d6c4c3f227f7117261c63b9e23a9", "3d3a621f852c42d97fd7260681e42508", "3432dd9ac0df80ef86eb80bd080f839b", "22aaeb4946ba6d2f2e27feb7dbb295de", "f61fbfb7aa1cd5dc8f70b055b51563e2", "f169d6d172dfb775895a5e2b1540c854", "9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f", "28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1", "bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66") or MD5 in~ ("1ab58838e5790efb22f2d35ab98c0b7d", "a7d7d6c4c3f227f7117261c63b9e23a9", "3d3a621f852c42d97fd7260681e42508", "3432dd9ac0df80ef86eb80bd080f839b", "22aaeb4946ba6d2f2e27feb7dbb295de", "f61fbfb7aa1cd5dc8f70b055b51563e2", "f169d6d172dfb775895a5e2b1540c854", "9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f", "28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1", "bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1ab58838e5790efb22f2d35ab98c0b7d", "a7d7d6c4c3f227f7117261c63b9e23a9", "3d3a621f852c42d97fd7260681e42508", "3432dd9ac0df80ef86eb80bd080f839b", "22aaeb4946ba6d2f2e27feb7dbb295de", "f61fbfb7aa1cd5dc8f70b055b51563e2", "f169d6d172dfb775895a5e2b1540c854", "9f5f2f0fb0a7f5aa9f16b9a7b6dad89f", "28cb7b261f4eb97e8a4b3b0d32f8def1", "bae82a15d1dbfb024617b9b56a8e5f66"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
